propositions: A check that asserts absence of a condition from subprocess/file/network output without verifying producer liveness (exit status, non-empty capture) cannot distinguish passing from the producer never running or emitting nothing.

Conversely, a check that reports a failure condition (e.g., all artifacts absent) based only on absent output cannot distinguish its failing verdict from the instrument receiving wrong input or the producer emitting nothing.

The fail-open antipattern appears in both test-oracle code (absence-based test assertions, grepped pytest output, orphaned log sweeps) and shipped error-handling code (silent lookup misses, unchecked subprocesses, pgrep patterns matching themselves).
The existing 'tests' and 'error-handling' code-review criteria must extend their language to cover fail-open/producer-liveness detection rather than creating a new criterion.

Calibration via live replay of nine pre-fix seeded diffs must verify each fires with a quoted finding naming the fail-open defect; all nine post-fix cases must yield zero findings after adding liveness checks.
Documentation of the pattern with two worked examples must be added to the code-review author guide (rebar explain review) since code-review criteria lack per-criterion explain surfaces.
